authored_assumptions: All geometry, hidden surfaces, mechanical details and material finishes are authored locally; no image-to-3D recovery or external assets are used.
The original blue/cream robot identity, all 17 bone names, parent relationships, major pivots, left-hand board and right-hand probe are retained.
Anatomical left is world +X, right is world -X, the rest-facing direction is -Y and units are meters with Z up before glTF export.
Closed body lofts and beveled panels are overlapping manufactured components, not one welded watertight outer surface.
The visible grip fingers and thumb are rigidly weighted to each hand bone; they are not independent finger joints or finger controls.
Board traces, pads and chip pins are static decorative geometry; probe motion and inspection are authored gestures, not contact-constrained manufacturing or a circuit simulation.
The four clips have matching authored endpoints as loop intent only. Rendered loop boundaries and state quality require downstream verification.
This general-profile revision uses real metallic-roughness PBR and richer geometry. It is not the matte diffuse weft-v1 deliverable and has not been validated against Weft.
Original bone rests are retained, while new shell surfaces, backside panels and small surface patterns are deliberate design assumptions.
Keyframe rotations and translations use model-rest axes; the backend converts them through bone rest bases.

HD textures are seeded, locally authored procedural patterns at native1024/2048 resolution, not neural output, reference-extracted texture maps or evidence of photorealism. Studio floor and exposure are render settings, not simulation geometry.

uv_repair.method: Per-loop geometric-plane UV projection for collapsed UVs or cancelling UV fans; other UV seams unchanged. Tangents are computed by Blender MikkTSpace, not replaced.

generation.local_compute: CPU, up to 4 threads; resource usage in job.json

origin: Agent-authored procedural geometry and skeletal keyframes; not neural reconstruction or an analytic fixture
preview_scope: portrait only; four exported clips still independently skin-tested

attachments.placement: Held by anatomical left hand/world +X, with its face toward the front camera at rest.
Held in anatomical right hand/world -X; points toward the workpiece at rest.

rig_verification.compatibility: Mapping checked against supplied target joint names only; target runtime not exercised.

motion.method: CPU linear-blend skinning at bounded key/midpoint samples

rig_verification.rest_pose: Authored default bone transforms. Blender Z-up/-Y-front exported to glTF Y-up/+Z-front.
rig_verification.visual_review: required; materials/textures are not rendered by this validator

rights: New locally authored shapes/materials; reference resemblance is not independent rights verification

states.meaning: An attentive settling sway with a small head tilt, tools held steadily at waist level.
Lifts the circuit board below the visor and studies it with a gentle head-and-body scan; the probe rests low.
Makes short precise probe gestures near the board's contact guide while the left hand steadies it. Copper tracks are fixed geometry, not newly manufactured marks.
Raises both tools into a wide open V with a small hop and preparatory knee bend; hands stay outside the face silhouette.

style: Designer retro-future character: shaped enamel shells, satin ivory armor, dark rubber seals, brushed metal collars and restrained warm brass accents.; native-HD procedural surface and grounded-studio edition
subject: A polished blue-and-ivory workshop robot with a friendly inset visor, metal joint hardware, a detailed circuit board and a precision probe.
